metadata.note: Quanah, Acme and Pacific Railway: Quanah - Acme - Paducah (1910) - Roaring Springs (1913) - MacBain - Floydada (1928), ~111 mi across the Texas Rolling Plains and up the Caprock. Chartered 1902 as the Acme, Red River and Northern (a plaster-plant switching road at Acme, no passenger evidence, not drawn), renamed QA&P 28 Jan 1909. The Frisco held stock control from c.1911 but the QA&P kept its own name, officers and trains to the end of passenger service, so there is no Rule 4 ownership split and every feature is QA&P colour. Until March 1931 QA&P trains reached Quanah over the Fort Worth & Denver City main; the QA&P's own Acme - Quanah line opened then - drawn as two era features. Passenger service (mixed trains by c.1950) is confirmed to 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide; its actual end is unknown.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, Quanah, Acme & Pacific Railway page (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines ~137468-137669; table dated c. April 30, 1950)
omitted: Matador branch (ex Motley County Railway, Matador Junction - Matador, 8 mi, 1914-1936): no source names a passenger or mixed train on it in any year - omitted, not drawn as freight. The 1952 Guide's 'Matador Line - Truck and Bus Service' note is road service after the 1936 abandonment.
Acme, Red River & Northern 1902-1909 and the Acme Tap / gypsite spurs: freight/industrial only (Rule 1).
Red River - Quanah (Frisco-owned, leased to QA&P 1914): passenger trains over it were the Frisco's Oklahoma City - Quanah trains; belongs in a Frisco layer.
Roaring Springs - MacBain 1913-1927 (stock-loading extension, no passenger evidence): drawn only from 1928.
not_yet_sourced: END YEAR [OPEN] on all five features: every drawable span ends 1951, the last CONFIRMED year (Feb 1952 Official Guide). No source dates the end of QA&P passenger/mixed service. Leads: Britton, 'The Quanah Route' (Texas A&M Press, 1990); Railroad Commission of Texas annual reports; Quanah Tribune-Chief / Floydada Hesperian / Paducah Post on the Portal to Texas History.
Paducah - Roaring Springs start: opened summer 1913, drawn from 1914; a 1913 timetable or newspaper would allow 1913.
Paducah start: a December 1909 train is possible but unproven; drawn from 1910.
Headway 1440 min (one train each way daily) is read from the c.1950 table only; earlier frequencies and the 1930s expedited 'Plainsman' are unsourced. avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.

Guide index dagger conflict: QA&P stations in the Feb 1952 index end 'Pact'/'Pac!', which could be the 'For freight only' dagger; the QA&P's own page prints passenger/mixed times, which were preferred. Unresolved.
Quanah - Acme own line: OHM labels the drawn way 'Oklahoma City and Texas Railroad' (1903); T27 dates the QA&P's own line to 1931. Conflict recorded.
ARR&N charter date conflict: 3 May 1902 (WP, AMR) vs 12 July 1902 (NRHP nomination). Not load-bearing.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1 from the start: no freight-only years or features drawn. Freight afterlife (overhead 'Quanah Route' freight to 1973; last train from Floydada 5 May 1981; BN merger 8 Jun 1981; abandonments 1979-87) is context only.

properties.geometry_quality: Quanah - Acme on the FORT WORTH & DENVER CITY main line (today BNSF, untagged active rail in OSM), traced 4.9 mi against a documented 4.9 mi (branchline.uk mileposts Quanah 8.1 - Acme 13.0 from Red River, 1911). No straight-line legs. This is the track QA&P trains used under FW&DC trackage rights until March 1931; it deliberately overlaps fort_worth_denver.geojson (the FW&DC's own feature) - that double-draw is correct, two companies' trains on one track. Not drawn: the FW&DC-built spur from the main to the QA&P's 1909 Quanah depot (location not pinned); the line ends at the FW&DC main at Quanah. ERA: drawn on the present BNSF alignment; any FW&DC line changes 1910-1930 not checked.

segments.note: QA&P (until 28 Jan 1909 Acme, Red River & Northern) trains ran Quanah - Acme over the FW&DC main under trackage rights (T27). Passenger service from 1910: track reached Paducah 9 Dec 1909 and the Paducah depot opened New Year's Day 1910 (Abandoned Rails); in the 1911 Official Guide (branchline.uk letter a = 1911G at Quanah and Acme). FW&DC terminated the rights c.1929-30; the QA&P's own Acme - Quanah line went into service March 1931 (T27), so QA&P trains were on this track for part of 1931 too - drawn only to 1930 so that 1931 is not claimed twice (the 1931 feature carries that year). Headway 1440 min = one train each way daily, read from the Feb 1952 Guide's c.1950 table; for every earlier year it is an ESTIMATE carried back by continuity (NOT SOURCED).
sources: Segment-level: start from branchline.uk 1911G letter at Quanah/Acme and Abandoned Rails (Paducah depot opened 1 Jan 1910); trackage-rights era and March 1931 changeover from txrrhistory.com Tower 27. Headway for these years NOT SOURCED (estimate).

properties.geometry_quality: QA&P's own 1931 Acme - Quanah line on its new right-of-way north of the FW&DC: drawn from OpenHistoricalMap way 202452981 (its east ~2 mi coincide with OSM way 189940822, a live BNSF 'Chickasha Subdivision' remnant tagged old_railway_operator=Frisco), 5.6 mi incl. a 0.2-km join at Acme to the razed QA&P grade. Up to 1.6 km north of the FW&DC, as T27 describes. Documented: the c.1950 Guide puts Lazare at MP 16.8 from Quanah against 15.4 mi via the FW&DC in 1911, implying the own line is ~1.4 mi longer than the 4.9-mi FW&DC route, i.e. ~6.3 mi. The trace is 5.6 mi; the shortfall is the Quanah end, which stops at the Frisco (Chickasha Sub) junction north-east of town rather than at the QA&P depot (not pinned). No straight-line legs. SOURCE CONFLICT: OHM names this way 'Oklahoma City and Texas Railroad', start_date 1903-03-29 - the Frisco's Red River - Quanah company. T27 dates the QA&P's own Acme - Quanah line to 1931 and says the 1903-1931 Acme connection was FW&DC track; the OHM label is taken to be a Frisco-lineage naming and the way is used as the 1931 QA&P line. Recorded, not resolved.

Read this feature as 'the road ran from Roaring Springs up to Floydada', not as an alignment.

segments.note: Roaring Springs - MacBain - Dougherty - Boothe Spur - Floydada.
